issues.claim: The criminal provisions sit alongside existing Title 18 offenses; takedown-notice provisions are codified at 47 U.S.C. § 223a
issues.issue: Codification is inaccurate. The TAKE IT DOWN Act amends 47 U.S.C. § 223 by adding subsection (h) containing BOTH the criminal prohibition AND related definitions. The criminal provision is in 47 U.S.C. § 223(h), NOT Title 18. § 223a covers the notice-and-removal platform obligation. The report inverts/conflates this.
issues.suggested_fix: Revise to: 'The criminal prohibition is codified at 47 U.S.C. § 223(h) (added by the Act to the Communications Act), and the platform notice-and-removal obligation is codified at 47 U.S.C. § 223a. The Act supplements — but does not reside in — existing Title 18 offenses.'

issues.claim: Platforms have until May 19, 2026 to comply, with FTC enforcement authority under the Federal Trade Commission Act
issues.issue: Hyperlink/text mismatch. Anchor text says 'Federal Trade Commission Act' but URL points to 47 U.S.C. § 223a, not the FTC Act (15 U.S.C. § 41 et seq.).
issues.suggested_fix: Change URL to 15 U.S.C. § 45 (FTC Act Section 5) since the Act treats platform violations as unfair or deceptive acts under Section 5.

issues.claim: The TAKE IT DOWN Act (S. 146, 119th Congress) was passed on April 28, 2025
issues.issue: April 28, 2025 is the House passage date; Senate passed S. 146 on February 13, 2025. 'Passed' without qualification is ambiguous.
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify: 'passed the House on April 28, 2025 (after Senate passage on February 13, 2025) and was signed into law on May 19, 2025.'

issues.claim: First-ever criminal conviction under the TAKE IT DOWN Act
issues.issue: Supported by USAO quote. Optionally note sentencing is pending to avoid confusion between guilty plea and final sentence.
issues.suggested_fix: Add '(conviction via guilty plea; sentencing pending)' on first use.
